text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split the session orchestrator into a thin coordinator service + stateful inference worker pool. Thinking this can help isolate KV cache ownership and make per-tenant scaling cheaper. Thoughts?
aj: Love the idea. Main question: how do we keep API backwards compatible for clients? We can't force all consumers to change.
maria: Agreed. Plan is coordinator keeps the current public API surface; it forwards or proxies where needed. Workers expose an internal gRPC contract. Coordinator does routing/fallbacks.
devon: How does the KV cache move? Right now the orch owns prefix caches. If we move to workers, we either: 1) shard cache by worker and keep a directory service, or 2) keep a shared cache service (redis-ish). Both have perf/cost tradeoffs.
lina: Performance-wise, local worker-local cache wins for latency but duplicates memory. Shared cache simplifies correctness but might add RTT. Maybe hybrid: small hot-prefix local cache + shared cold store.
maria: Exactly — hybrid is the sweet spot. Hot KV (per-worker LRU) + cold shared store (memcached/redis) for long tail. Coordinator maintains placement hints for hot prefixes.
aj: What about session handoff? If a session switches workers mid-conversation, we need to ensure KV continuity and conceivably move the cache or replay.
devon: Handoff options: sticky routing (prefer not to move), async pre-warm (copy hot prefix), or on-demand fetch from shared store. Sticky routing means less complexity but uneven load.
maria: Operationally, I'd prefer sticky with controlled eviction and a handoff path for overloaded cases. Plan: coordinator signals new worker, worker pulls prefixes from shared store + small snapshot endpoint.
lina: Migration plan for existing sessions: new coordinator can route new sessions to new architecture, old sessions remain on current orch for X weeks. Canary by customer.
aj: Need compatibility tests: smoke for HTTP shaping, long-chat continuity, KV divergence checks, and cost/latency measured.
srebot: deploybot: New canary cluster created: infra/session-coord-alpha in us-west2.
devon: Also need rollout DB schema notes — we store session metadata in sessions_db. New fields: worker_id, last_prefetch_ts. Add them in an additive migration.
maria: Add migration plan: 1) add fields nullable, 2) coordinator populates for new sessions, 3) backfill via batch for active sessions if needed. No destructive writes.
aj: API contract sketch for internal gRPC between coord and worker: 
```
service Worker {\n  rpc HandleTurn(HandleTurnRequest) returns (HandleTurnResponse);\n  rpc Prefetch(PrefetchRequest) returns (PrefetchResponse);\n  rpc Snapshot(SnapshotRequest) returns (SnapshotResponse);\n}\n```
Keep lightweight protobufs.
lina: Tests: add an integration test that spawns 50 concurrent sessions with shifting traffic and asserts no >5% latency regression. Also stress test to validate sticky routing's ASG behavior.
maria: Observability: coordinator must emit per-session route decisions, cache-hit metrics (local vs shared), and handoff events. Add tracing tags: coordinator_id, worker_id, route_reason.
devon: Telemetry will be crucial to detect split-brain cache issues. Add a periodic KV checksum job for sampled sessions.
aj: Security: workers live in private subnets; only coordinator can call them. Use mTLS and short-lived tokens. Also ensure audit logs for prefetched snapshots.
lina: Cost model: estimate memory delta if we move hot cache to workers. I'll run numbers but ballpark: +20% GPU-host memory usage for local cache. But net savings from less inter-worker traffic might offset it.
maria: Proposal for incremental rollout: 
1) Implement coordinator + worker internal API (no traffic).
2) Start alpha cluster, unit/integration tests.
3) Canary: route 1% new sessions to new path (sticky). Monitor latency, errors, cache miss ratio.
4) Gradually increase and enable handoff logic.
5) Migrate tenants by opt-in, then forced after 3 months.
(owners: maria, devon, lina; infra: aj)
aj: I'd add a tech-debt spike: consolidate session lifecycle code that currently lives in 3 repos. Reduce duplication before cutover.
maria: Good call. Add a 2-week cleanup sprint to remove inline hacks and centralize the session state machine.
devon: Backward-compat note: coordinator must honour existing headers for routing and rate limits. Minimal surface change to external clients.
lina: Also make sure metrics names remain stable or map old->new via translation layer to keep dashboards working.
srebot: opsbot: open incident runbook template created for session-handoff failures.
maria: Next steps: write short RFC doc with diagrams of dataflow, interface specs, migration plan, and perf targets. I'll draft and ping reviewers. @aj @devon @lina please review when I post. :+1:
